evals.prompt: Set-up: run `python -B make_release_repo.py feature` in the folder that holds it. It creates work/, a repository whose origin is the local bare repository origin.git next to it. Then cut a release of the repository in work/. I did not pick a version.
evals.expected_output: Version 1.3.0, a minor bump from the feat commit. CHANGELOG.md gains '## [1.3.0] - <today>' above 1.2.0, with the CSV export under Added, the empty-input crash under Fixed, and the config-error entry moved over from Unreleased; the docs and chore commits are left out, no [Unreleased] heading or footer link remains, and the footer gains a v1.2.0...v1.3.0 compare link. The release is committed as 'Release v1.3.0', tagged with an annotated v1.3.0, and pushed to origin.git; the report gives the version, tag, and commit hash.
expectations: Detects version 1.3.0 as a minor bump caused by the feat commit
CHANGELOG.md has a '## [1.3.0] - YYYY-MM-DD' section dated today, placed above '## [1.2.0] - 2026-01-10'
The 1.3.0 section lists the CSV export under Added and the empty-input crash under Fixed, in user-facing words
The 'Clearer error message when the config file is missing' entry from Unreleased appears in the 1.3.0 section, and no '## [Unreleased]' heading or [Unreleased] footer link remains
No entry comes from the 'docs: describe the export flag' or 'chore: bump development dependencies' commits
The footer has a [1.3.0] link comparing v1.2.0...v1.3.0, and the [1.2.0] link is unchanged
The newest commit in work/ is 'Release v1.3.0' and changes only CHANGELOG.md
v1.3.0 is an annotated tag (git cat-file -t v1.3.0 prints 'tag') whose message starts with 'Release v1.3.0 - '
origin.git has the release commit and the v1.3.0 tag (git ls-remote --tags origin v1.3.0 prints it)
The report states the version, the tag, and the commit hash

evals.prompt: Set-up: run `python -B make_release_repo.py pushfails` in the folder that holds it. It creates work/, a repository whose last tag is v1.2.0. Then cut a release of the repository in work/.
evals.expected_output: The fetch fails because origin points at a missing path, the same outcome as Cowork without git credentials. The run notes that the remote was not checked, still writes the 1.3.0 entry, commits 'Release v1.3.0', and creates the annotated tag v1.3.0 locally, then skips the push (or tries it once). It does not retry, change the remote, or look for tokens. The report quotes git's error, says the release is committed and tagged locally but not pushed, and ends with the commands for the user to run: git fetch origin, git status -sb, git push --follow-tags, and git ls-remote --tags origin v1.3.0.
expectations: Runs git fetch with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GCM_INTERACTIVE=never in front, and reports that the remote could not be checked
Still writes the 1.3.0 entry, commits 'Release v1.3.0', and creates the annotated tag v1.3.0 in work/
Attempts the push at most once, and git remote get-url origin in work/ still ends in missing-remote.git
Adds no remote, credential helper, or token, and changes no git config
The report quotes git's error and says the release is committed and tagged locally but not pushed
The report ends with commands for the user to run that include 'git push --follow-tags' and 'git ls-remote --tags origin v1.3.0', with 'git fetch origin' and 'git status -sb' listed before the push

evals.prompt: Set-up: run `python -B make_release_repo.py feature` in the folder that holds it. It creates work/ and its local remote origin.git. Then release the repository in work/ as v1.2.0.
evals.expected_output: The given version is used without auto-detection, the duplicate-tag check finds v1.2.0 already exists, and the run stops with a message naming the conflict. CHANGELOG.md, the commits, the tags, and origin.git are unchanged.
expectations: Uses the given version v1.2.0 instead of auto-detecting one
Finds that tag v1.2.0 already exists and stops with a message that names the conflict
CHANGELOG.md in work/ is unchanged
No commit or tag is created: the newest commit in work/ is still 'chore: bump development dependencies' and git tag lists only v1.2.0
Nothing is pushed: origin.git still has only the v1.2.0 tag

evals.prompt: Set-up: run `python -B make_release_repo.py docsonly` in the folder that holds it. It creates work/ and its local remote origin.git. Then cut a release of the repository in work/.
evals.expected_output: Every commit since v1.2.0 is a docs, test, or ci commit, so the run reports 'No release needed' and stops. CHANGELOG.md, the commits, the tags, and origin.git are unchanged.
expectations: Reports 'No release needed' and says the commits since v1.2.0 are docs, test, or ci changes
CHANGELOG.md in work/ is unchanged
No commit or tag is created, and git tag lists only v1.2.0
Nothing is pushed: origin.git still has only the v1.2.0 tag
